subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0024’s shared locale-context and compatibility contracts as the product direction for runtime, Gateway, channels, and localized capability metadata?
rationale: The RFC intentionally establishes cross-surface policy and future compatibility constraints rather than documenting an already accepted implementation; source review cannot determine the desired product boundary or accountable owners.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded v1 foundation
options.body: Approve a narrowly scoped foundation with named owners for locale precedence, Gateway compatibility, safety-copy review, and plugin metadata boundaries before implementation proceeds.

options.title: Defer the cross-product contract
options.body: Keep the RFC draft open but do not treat it as accepted direction until the affected surface owners agree on scope and ownership.

options.title: Narrow to independent surface RFCs
options.body: Split the runtime, Gateway, channel, and metadata decisions if one global contract is not the preferred governance model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded v1 foundation
recommendation.body: Approve a narrowly scoped foundation with named owners for locale precedence, Gateway compatibility, safety-copy review, and plugin metadata boundaries before implementation proceeds.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal author is the only person evidenced in the available RFC history and can route the requested decision to the relevant product and surface owners.
